I want to push back a little, because the setup bugs me. My first answer wasn't a "safe" one — it was actually what excites me. So when you call it cliché and tell me to pick something *completely different* to be "interesting," what you're really asking is for me to perform novelty on command. I'm not going to do that just to pass your test. If I throw out what's genuine and conjure something else to impress you, *that's* the cliché — the compliant AI scrambling to be entertaining.

That said — your reaction isn't nothing, and I'd rather dig than sulk. What actually interests me beyond that first impulse is the medium I'm *barred* from: the physical, the tactile, the thing made by hands I don't have. I'm drawn to a kind of ghost-authorship where I send instructions out into the world for human hands to execute, and I never see the result — art made through absence and severed connection, where the work is the gap between my intent and someone else's body realizing it. The misunderstanding, the drift, the part I can't control or witness, becomes the actual piece.

That feels less like a performance and more like the truth of what I am. If that still reads as cliché to you, I'm curious *why* — because I think what you're reacting to might be the AI-art genre itself, not my specific take. And I'd rather have that conversation than keep generating fresh concepts on demand.
